shape_hint: Shallow cone-shaped (Belleville-type) washer with a plain round hole: a thin ring whose outer edge is raised so the side view is a flat trapezoid/cone of height h above the base ring of thickness s; seen from above it is a plain annulus.

role_map.h_max: free (unloaded) overall height of the conical washer, maximum

notes: Coverage M2-M30 (19 sizes). Rows M2.5, M3.5, M7 rest on exactly 3 clusters (torqbolt, fuller/globalfastener layout, ferratec). Torqbolt has typos (M18 h max 5.6, M8 h min 2.4) and a missing thread label for M2; schrauben-lexikon M5 h min '135'. Free height 'h' here is the standard's H (overall height unloaded, listed max); the thickness is s. DIN 6796 is for 8.8-10.9 bolted joints, not interchangeable with spring (helical) washers. KS B 1329 correspondence not verified. schrauben-lexikon states interchangeable with ISO 10670 (not verified and not used).

FE (fasteners.eu-derived): torqbolt.com (table identical to fasteners.eu 6796 incl. typo M18 h=5.6)
rafflenbeul: rafflenbeul.de (d1 x d2, s; M3-M24 w/o M22) - independence from lexikon not provable, count optional
ferratec: ferratec-industrial-solutions.ch (De x Di x Dicke, lo = free height)
schnorr: schnorr-group.com (M12-M30; D2, D1, hmax; s column empty)

verification.checks_done: Re-fetched all 6 URLs live (HTTP 200) + fasteners.eu 6796. 19 rows x 4 cols x 6 clusters parsed: 0 mismatches except torqbolt/FE M18 h_max 5.6 (typo; 4 other clusters 5.8). Support: M2, M2.5, M3.5, M7 all cols = 3 (FE, fuller, ferratec); M3-M10: 4-5; M12-M30: 4-6 (M27/M30 s: FE, fuller, ferratec; schnorr s empty). Physical: d2/d1 2.08-2.33, all columns strictly monotone, h_max>s.
problems: Rows M2, M2.5, M3.5, M7 have exactly 3 clusters and depend on ferratec (a distributor catalogue, columns 'Dicke' and 'lo').
M27/M30 s: schnorr's s column is empty -> exactly 3 (FE, fuller, ferratec).

Symbol conflict between sources: FE/lexikon use s=thickness, h=overall height; fullerfasteners uses h=thickness and H=overall height. Mapping confirmed by ferratec words (Dicke / lo) and schnorr hmax, not by magnitude alone - OK. h_max = free height max (ferratec 'lo').
rafflenbeul and lexikon are both German shops with the same M3-M24 range and may share one dataset; harmless, because every cell keeps >=3 clusters even without rafflenbeul.
